original_text: THE LOOK-ELSEWHERE COST OF THE GPS-STYLE CORRELATION SEARCH, computed and to be written into the hydroacoustics brief. A matched-filter search over a time window has roughly 2*W*B independent trials. At a +/-1 h window and 30 Hz band that is 216,000 trials, requiring 5.3 sigma per trial for a 1% global false alarm; +/-2 h at 30 Hz gives 432,000 and 5.5 sigma; narrowing to 8 Hz or to +/-15 min gives ~54,000-57,600 and only 5.1 sigma, so a 4x trial reduction buys just 0.2 sigma. MULTI-SITE COINCIDENCE IS THE LEVER THAT WORKS: requiring a second station consistent within +/-30 s of the predicted lag cuts the trial space 120x (4.4 sigma) and within +/-10 s cuts it 360x (4.1 sigma) - worth about a full sigma. Set against Duncan's 20-30 dB penalty, the honest expectation is that a single-site search cannot clear 5.3 sigma.

original_text: WHERE TAU MATTERS, COMPUTED and now in the hydroacoustics brief: the first acoustic-mode cutoff f_c = c/4H is 0.125/0.094/0.075/0.063 Hz at 3,000/4,000/5,000/6,000 m, i.e. periods 8.0/10.7/13.3/16.0 s. A source of duration tau rolls off above ~1/tau. SOFAR: any plausible tau from 0.05 to 10 s rolls off between 20 and 0.1 Hz, squarely inside the IMS hydrophone band, so tau shapes the source spectrum directly and matters a great deal. AGW: for tau below ~10 s the impact is effectively impulsive for the whole AGW band and excitation depends on total impulse and displaced volume, not tau—so whether tau matters to AGW is itself a function of tau, with the threshold set by DEPTH; compute f_c at the candidate impact depth, not at a nominal 4,000 m. Tau does not change the look-elsewhere trial count (set by window x bandwidth, ~432,000 at +/-1 h and 30 Hz); it changes the time-bandwidth product tau*B that sets per-trial processing gain (30 at tau 1 s and B 30 Hz, 300 at tau 10 s).

original_text: The hydroacoustic 95% upper limit is an OUTPUT of injection-recovery, not a known number; it reads 'a source at or above level L would have been detected with probability 0.95; nothing was seen; therefore the source was below L.' Only one of the three ways to change it is real: lowering confidence to 90% or 68% tightens the stated limit cosmetically while weakening the guarantee; improving the detector (matched filtering, coincidence) genuinely lowers L; reporting the whole power curve plus the likelihood ratio makes the limit one point on a curve. Pete's concern about being over-conservative on near-noise signals belongs at the detection threshold, not at the upper limit, because the likelihood ratio shows a near-noise signal even when it fails every threshold.

original_text: Hydro module uncertainty conventions and where they come from. Pick sd: 10 s (PICK_S in kadri_table1_test.py). This is a module convention with no published source found. IMOS clock sd: 2 s (declared).
